nahhas-meani:22-22.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَمَا يَسْتَوِي ٱلأَحْيَآءُ وَلاَ ٱلأَمْوَاتُ﴾.
That is, those who reason and the ignorant.
What is meant by "the living" (al-aḥyāʾ) is: those whose hearts are alive with faith and knowledge.
And "the dead" (al-amwāt): those whose hearts are dead because unbelief has overcome them, until they no longer distinguish guidance from error.

nahhas-meani:24-24.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَإِن مِّنْ أُمَّةٍ إِلاَّ خَلاَ فِيهَا نَذِيرٌ﴾.
That is, a prophet passed among it before.

nahhas-meani:27-27.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلْجِبَالِ جُدَدٌ بِيضٌ وَحُمْرٌ مُّخْتَلِفٌ أَلْوَانُهَا وَغَرَابِيبُ سُودٌ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: that is, different colours, i.e. white, red and black. He said: and al-judad are the tracks (streaks).
Abū Jaʿfar said: Abū ʿUbayda said: al-ghirbīb is the intensely black.

nahhas-meani:28-28.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَٱلدَّوَآبِّ وَٱلأَنْعَامِ مُخْتَلِفٌ أَلْوَانُهُ كَذَلِكَ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: that is, and among people there are the white, the red and the black.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى ٱللَّهَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ ٱلْعُلَمَاءُ﴾.
That is, those who know His power over whatever He wills; whoever knows that is certain that He will punish disobedience, and so fears Him.
As ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى ٱللَّهَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ ٱلْعُلَمَاءُ﴾.
He said: those who know that Allah has power over all things.
And in the ḥadīth: (Fear of Allah suffices as knowledge, and being deluded about Him suffices as ignorance).

nahhas-meani:32-32.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿ثُمَّ أَوْرَثْنَا ٱلْكِتَابَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱصْطَفَيْنَا مِنْ عِبَادِنَا فَمِنْهُمْ ظَالِمٌ لِّنَفْسِهِ وَمِنْهُمْ مُّقْتَصِدٌ وَمِنْهُمْ سَابِقٌ بِٱلْخَيْرَاتِ بِإِذُنِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
It has been said that the one who is saved is the moderate (al-muqtaṣid) and the foremost (al-sābiq), and that His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ يَدْخُلُونَهَا﴾ is for the moderate and the foremost. This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, ʿIkrima, al-Ḥasan and Qatāda.
Ibn ʿUyayna related from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ ظَالِمٌ لِّنَفْسِهِ﴾ — he said: an unbeliever.
And from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: ﴿الكِتَابُ﴾: every Book that was sent down.
And from him: all of them are the community of Muḥammad ﷺ — in the narration of Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa from him; and this is the most fitting of what has been said about it.
Al-Thawrī related from Jābir, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ثُمَّ أَوْرَثْنَا ٱلْكِتَابَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱصْطَفَيْنَا مِنْ عِبَادِنَا﴾ to the end of the verse.
He said: this is like His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَأَصْحَابُ المَيْمَنَةِ مَا أَصْحَابُ المَيْمَنَة. وَأَصْحَابُ المَشْأَمَةِ مَا أَصْحَابُ المَشْأَمَةِ. وَالسَّابِقُونَ السَّابِقُونَ أُوْلَئِكَ المُقَرَّبُونَ﴾.
He said: so two groups are saved.
Mujāhid said: ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ ظَالِمٌ لِّنَفْسِهِ﴾ are the Companions of the Left; ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مُّقْتَصِدٌ وَمِنْهُمْ سَابِقٌ بِٱلْخَيْرَاتِ بِإِذُنِ ٱللَّهِ﴾ — the foremost among all people.
ʿIkrima said: ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ ظَالِمٌ لِّنَفْسِهِ﴾ is as He said: ﴿فَذُوقُوا فَمَا للِظَّالِميِنَ مِنْ نَصِيرٍ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda said: ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ ظَالِمٌ لِّنَفْسِهِ﴾ is the hypocrite.
Qatāda said: ﴿الكتابُ﴾ is the testimony that there is no god but Allah.
And it has been said: all three groups are saved. This was said by ʿUmar, Abū al-Dardāʾ, Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī and Kaʿb al-Aḥbār.
ʿUthmān said: they are the people of our desert — meaning the one who wrongs himself.
ʿUmar said: our foremost is foremost, our moderate is saved, and our wrongdoer is forgiven.
Abū al-Dardāʾ said: the foremost enters Paradise without reckoning; (the moderate) is given an easy reckoning; and (the one who wrongs himself) is taken to account and then saved — and that is His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَقَالُوا الحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَذْهَبَ عَنَّا الحَزَنَ﴾.
Kaʿb said: this community is in three groups, all of them in Paradise. Then he recited ﴿ثُمَّ أَوْرَثْنَا ٱلْكِتَابَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱصْطَفَيْنَا مِنْ عِبَادِنَا فَمِنْهُمْ ظَالِمٌ لِّنَفْسِهِ﴾ up to His saying ﴿جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ يَدْخُلُونَهَا﴾ and said: they have entered it, by the Lord of the Kaʿba.
And after this comes [what is] for the unbelievers.

nahhas-meani:36-36.t:
That is His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَهُمْ نَارُ جَهَنَّمَ لاَ يُقْضَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ فَيَمُوتُواْ﴾.
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: men are of four kinds: the generous, the miserly, the extravagant and the moderate.
The generous is the one who directs both the share of his Hereafter and the share of his worldly life, together, towards his Hereafter.
The miserly is the one who gives neither of them its due.
The extravagant is the one who gathers both of them for this world.
The moderate is the one who gives each of them its share, i.e. his deeds are measured (qaṣd), not strenuous. [Translator's note: the source reads «ليس يمجتهد», apparently a misprint for «ليس بمجتهد» "not strenuous"; translated accordingly.]
Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: the meaning of ﴿أَذْهَبَ عَنَّا الحَزَنَ﴾ is: worry over livelihood, fear of the punishment, and the expectation of death.
And all that he said has come in the tafsīr, so it is general for every kind of grief.
Al-muqāma and al-maqām are the same; and al-naṣab is fatigue.
Al-lughūb is exhaustion; and al-laghūb, with fatḥa on the lām, is that from which one becomes exhausted.
Al-Ḥasan read: ﴿لا يُقْضَى عَلَيْهِمْ فَيَمُوتُونَ﴾.
The meaning according to his reading is: death is not decreed for them, and they do not die.

nahhas-meani:37-37.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿أَوَلَمْ نُعَمِّرْكُمْ مَّا يَتَذَكَّرُ فِيهِ مَن تَذَكَّرَ﴾.
Abū Hurayra and Ibn ʿAbbās said: sixty years.
And from him [Ibn ʿAbbās] also: forty.
And this is more likely, because at forty the intellect reaches its full extent, and what is before and after that falls short of it — and Allah, Majestic and Mighty, knows best.
Al-Ḥasan also said: forty; and it is said that a seventeen-year-old is included in it.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَجَآءَكُمُ ٱلنَّذِيرُ﴾.
Ibn Zayd said: the Prophet ﷺ.
And it has been said: it means grey hair.
The first is held by more; and the meaning according to the second is: until you grew grey — and this is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās.

nahhas-meani:39-39.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَ ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَكُمْ خَلاَئِفَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
That is, you succeed those who were before you, and take warning from what befell them.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَمَن كَفَرَ فَعَلَيْهِ كُفْرُهُ﴾.
That is, the recompense of his unbelief.
﴿وَلاَ يَزِيدُ ٱلْكَافِرِينَ كُفْرُهُمْ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ إِلاَّ مَقْتاً﴾.
Al-maqt is the most intense loathing.

nahhas-meani:40-40.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ شُرَكَآءَكُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
The meaning, according to Sībawayh: Inform me about those whom you call upon besides Allah — by way of making them stop and consider (tawqīf).
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿أَرُونِي مَاذَا خَلَقُواْ مِنَ ٱلأَرْضِ أَمْ لَهُمْ شِرْكٌ فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ﴾.
That is: did you worship them because they created something of the earth? Or do they have a share in the creation of the heavens?
﴿أَمْ آتَيْنَاهُمْ كِتَاباً﴾ granting partnership, ﴿فَهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَيِّنَةٍ مِّنْهُ﴾ — that is, upon clear proofs from it?

nahhas-meani:41-41.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُمْسِكُ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ أَن تَزُولاَ﴾.
The meaning according to the Basrans: lest they cease (literally "from dislike that they cease"), just as He, Glorified is He, said: ﴿وَاسْأَلِ القَرْيَةَ﴾. [Translator's note: i.e. a muḍāf is omitted, as "the people of" is omitted in «واسأل القرية».]
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَلَئِن زَالَتَآ إِنْ أَمْسَكَهُمَا مِنْ أَحَدٍ مِّن بَعْدِهِ﴾.
The meaning may be: at their ceasing on the Day of Resurrection.
And it may be that this is said even though they do not cease; "إنْ" is in the sense of "ما" (not). It resembles His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَلَئِنْ أَرْسَلْنَا رِيحَاً فَرَأَوْهُ مُصْفَرَّاً﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: there is a question about the verse. It is said: this is a context of power, so how did He say ﴿إِنَّهُ كَانَ حَلِيماً غَفُوراً﴾?
The answer: when they said ﴿اتَّخَذَ الرَّحْمَنُ وَلَدَاً﴾, the mountains nearly ceased, the heavens nearly split apart and the earth nearly collapsed, because of the enormity of what they said; so Allah, Majestic and Mighty, held them still, delayed their punishment and was forbearing towards them. That is His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿إِنَّهُ كَانَ حَلِيماً غَفُوراً﴾.

nahhas-meani:42-42.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿لَئِن جَآءَهُمْ نَذِيرٌ لَّيَكُونُنَّ أَهْدَىٰ مِنْ إِحْدَى ٱلأُمَمِ﴾.
The meaning of ﴿أَهْدَىٰ مِنْ إِحْدَى ٱلأُمَمِ﴾ is: [better guided than] the Jews and the Christians.

nahhas-meani:43-43.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿ٱسْتِكْبَاراً فِي ٱلأَرْضِ وَمَكْرَ ٱلسَّيِّىءِ وَلاَ يَحِيقُ ٱلْمَكْرُ ٱلسَّيِّىءُ إِلاَّ بِأَهْلِهِ﴾.
﴿وَمَكْرَ ٱلسَّيِّىءِ﴾: it has been said: that is, and the plotting of unbelief.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَلاَ يَحِيقُ ٱلْمَكْرُ ٱلسَّيِّىءُ إِلاَّ بِأَهْلِهِ﴾ — that is, the harm of the evil plot befalls none but its people, i.e. those who plot it.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَهَلْ يَنظُرُونَ إِلاَّ سُنَّتَ آلأَوَّلِينَ﴾? [verse 43].
That is: do they await anything but the way [of Allah] with the former peoples in punishment when they disbelieved?

nahhas-meani:45-45.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلَوْ يُؤَاخِذُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلنَّاسَ بِمَا كَسَبُواْ مَا تَرَكَ عَلَىٰ ظَهْرِهَا مِن دَآبَّةٍ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: it means people specifically.
And from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd there is what indicates that it means people and others.
He said: the dung beetle was nearly punished for the sin of the children of Adam. Then he recited ﴿وَلَوْ يُؤَاخِذُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلنَّاسَ بِمَا كَسَبُواْ مَا تَرَكَ عَلَىٰ ظَهْرِهَا مِن دَآبَّةٍ﴾, the verse.
Qatāda said: that was done in the days of Noah ﷺ.
* And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿عَلَىٰ ظَهْرِهَا﴾.
It has been said: it is known that the meaning is "on the surface of the earth".
Abū Jaʿfar said: it is better that the pronoun refer back to what has already been mentioned, in His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَسِيرُوا فِي الأَرْضِ﴾.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَجَلُهُمْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ بِعِبَادِهِ بَصِيراً﴾.
﴿فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَجَلُهُمْ﴾: that is, the term of their punishment.
﴿فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ بِعِبَادِهِ بَصِيراً﴾: that is, All-Seeing of what each group of them deserves.

nahhas-meani:1-1.t:
Among that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلْحَمْدُ للَّهِ فَاطِرِ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: I did not know what ﴿فاطرُ﴾ meant until two Bedouins brought a dispute to me over a well, and one of them said: I فَطَرْتُها, that is, I began it.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿جَاعِلِ ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةِ رُسُلاً أُوْلِيۤ أَجْنِحَةٍ مَّثْنَىٰ وَثُلاَثَ وَرُبَاعَ﴾.
The messengers among them are "Gabriel, Michael, Isrāfīl and the Angel of Death", may Allah bless them.
* His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿أُوْلِيۤ أَجْنِحَةٍ مَّثْنَىٰ وَثُلاَثَ وَرُبَاعَ﴾, that is, possessors of wings: two by two, three by three and four by four, on each side.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿يَزِيدُ فِي ٱلْخَلْقِ مَا يَشَآءُ﴾.
That is, He adds to the creation of the angels whatever He wills.
Al-Zuhrī said: ﴿يَزِيدُ فِي ٱلْخَلْقِ مَا يَشَآءُ﴾: a beautiful voice.
The first is preferable.

nahhas-meani:2-2.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَّا يَفْتَحِ ٱللَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ مِن رَّحْمَةٍ فَلاَ مُمْسِكَ لَهَا﴾.
That is, whatever Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, brings of rain and provision, no one is able to turn it back.
Qatāda said: ﴿مِن رَّحْمَةٍ﴾: of good; no one is able to withhold it.

nahhas-meani:3-3.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿لاَ إِلَـٰهَ إِلاَّ هُوَ فَأَنَّىٰ تُؤْفَكُونَ﴾.
That is: so how are you turned away from [affirming His] oneness and from belief in the resurrection, after the proofs and the signs?

nahhas-meani:5-5.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلاَ تَغُرَّنَّكُمُ ٱلْحَيَاةُ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَلاَ يَغُرَّنَّكُمْ بِٱللَّهِ ٱلْغَرُورُ﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: ﴿ٱلْغَرُورُ﴾ is Satan.
Shuʿba narrated from Simāk ibn Ḥarb: ﴿الغُرُورُ﴾ with ḍamma on the ghayn.
It was said: This is not permissible, because one only says غرَّه غرَّاً, and the maṣdar (verbal noun) hardly ever comes on the pattern "فُعُول" with a transitive verb except anomalously.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is possible that "غُرُور" is the plural of غارّ (deceiver), or the plural of غِرّ (one who is deceived); or it may be likened to their saying نَهَكَه المرضُ نُهُوكاً (illness wore him down) and لَزِمَه لُزُوماً (it clung to him).

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَفَمَن زُيِّنَ لَهُ سُوۤءُ عَمَلِهِ فَرَآهُ حَسَناً﴾.
The answer (complement) is omitted because the hearer knows it. The meaning may be: Is one to whom the evil of his deed has been made to seem fair like one whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has guided? And what indicates this omitted [part] would be ﴿فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُضِلُّ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهْدِي مَن يَشَآءُ﴾.
And the meaning may be: Is one to whom the evil of his deed has been made to seem fair [one over whom] your soul should waste away [in grief]?
And what indicates it would be ﴿فَلاَ تَذْهَبْ نَفْسُكَ عَلَيْهِمْ حَسَرَاتٍ﴾.

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَن كَانَ يُرِيدُ ٱلْعِزَّةَ فَلِلَّهِ ٱلْعِزَّةُ جَمِيعاً﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid, who said: Whoever seeks might through the worship of idols.
Al-Farrāʾ said: Whoever seeks to know [to whom] might [belongs].
Then He said: ﴿فَلِلَّهِ ٱلْعِزَّةُ جَمِيعاً﴾, that is, Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, gives might to whomever He wills through obedience to Him.
Qatāda said: So let him seek might through obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The most fitting of them is the first, because in the verses before it the polytheists were rebuked for worshipping idols, so it is more fitting that this one too be of the kind that urges abandoning that.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إِلَيْهِ يَصْعَدُ ٱلْكَلِمُ ٱلطَّيِّبُ وَٱلْعَمَلُ ٱلصَّالِحُ يَرْفَعُهُ﴾.
Concerning its meaning there are three views:
A- Among them is what Bakr ibn Sahl narrated to us; he said: Abū Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, from Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His saying ﴿إِلَيْهِ يَصْعَدُ ٱلْكَلِمُ ٱلطَّيِّبُ وَٱلْعَمَلُ ٱلصَّالِحُ يَرْفَعُهُ﴾: he said: The good speech is the remembrance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and ﴿ٱلْعَمَلُ ٱلصَّالِحُ﴾ is the performance of His obligations.
So whoever remembers Allah, Glorified is He, while performing His obligations, his deed carries the remembrance of Allah and it ascends to Allah, Glorified is He.
And whoever remembers Allah but does not perform His obligations, his speech is turned back upon his deed, and [his deed] has the greater claim on him.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Likewise said al-Ḥasan, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Mujāhid, Abū al-ʿĀliya and al-Ḍaḥḥāk; they said: The righteous deed raises the good speech.
Al-Ḥasan said: If there is good speech but an evil deed, the saying is turned back upon the deed, and your deed has a greater claim on you than your saying.
B- Shahr ibn Ḥawshab said: ﴿إِلَيْهِ يَصْعَدُ ٱلْكَلِمُ ٱلطَّيِّبُ﴾ is the Qurʾān; ﴿وَٱلْعَمَلُ ٱلصَّالِحُ يَرْفَعُهُ﴾: the Qurʾān [raises it].
C- Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: And the righteous deed — Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, raises it.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Qatāda's view is not far-fetched in meaning, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, raises deeds.
And the meaning of Shahr ibn Ḥawshab's view is that the righteous deed does not benefit you except together with tawḥīd (affirming Allah's oneness), so it is as though tawḥīd raises it.
However, the first view is the most fitting and the soundest of them, because of the high standing of those who held it, and because it is more fitting in Arabic: the readers have the nominative for العمل; had the meaning been "and the righteous deed, Allah raises it" or "and the righteous deed, the good word raises it", the preferred choice would have been the accusative for العمل. We do not know of anyone who read it in the accusative, except something narrated from ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar, who said: Some people read it ﴿والعملَ الصالحَ يرفعهُ﴾.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يَمْكُرُونَ ٱلسَّيِّئَاتِ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ شَدِيدٌ وَمَكْرُ أُوْلَئِكَ هُوَ يَبُورُ﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda: ﴿يَبُورُ﴾: he said: comes to ruin.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has made this plotting clear in His saying: ﴿وَإذْ يَمْكُرُ بِكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِيُثْبِتُوكَ﴾.
Qays narrated from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid: ﴿وَمَكْرُ أُوْلَئِكَ هُوَ يَبُورُ﴾: he said: showing off (riyāʾ).

nahhas-meani:11-11.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا يُعَمَّرُ مِن مُّعَمَّرٍ وَلاَ يُنقَصُ مِنْ عُمُرِهِ إِلاَّ فِي كِتَابٍ﴾.
Concerning the meaning of this verse there are [several] views:
A- Among the best of them and the closest to the apparent sense of the revelation is the view of al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said: "Whomever I have decreed to be given long life until old age overtakes him, or to be given a life short of that — all of that is by decree, and all is in a Book."
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning on this view is: ﴿وَمَا يُعَمَّرُ مِن مُّعَمَّرٍ﴾, that is, an aged one — and "so-and-so is مُعَمَّر" means old — ﴿وَلاَ يُنقَصُ﴾ another ﴿مِنْ عُمُرِهِ﴾, from the lifespan of the aged one, except by a decree from Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
B- ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib narrated from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿وَمَا يُعَمَّرُ مِن مُّعَمَّرٍ وَلاَ يُنقَصُ مِنْ عُمُرِهِ إِلاَّ فِي كِتَابٍ﴾:
He said: His lifespan is written as so many years, so many months and so many days; then it is written: a day has been subtracted from his life, a month has been subtracted from his life, a year has been subtracted from his life — in another record — until he completes his term and dies.
C- Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: What has passed of his life is the subtraction, and what is yet to come is that for which he is given life.
D- Al-Zuhrī narrated from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, from Kaʿb al-Aḥbār, that he said, when ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was stabbed: "If he were to supplicate to Allah, He would extend his term." The Muslims objected to him about that and said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, says: ﴿فإذَا جَاءَ أَجَلُهُمْ لاَ يَسْتَأْخِرُونَ سَاعَةً وَلا يَسْتَقْدِمُونَ﴾. He said: And Allah, Exalted is He, says: ﴿وَمَا يُعَمَّرُ مِن مُّعَمَّرٍ وَلاَ يُنقَصُ مِنْ عُمُرِهِ إِلاَّ فِي كِتَابٍ﴾.
E- Al-Zuhrī said: We hold that it may be deferred as long as the term has not arrived; but when the term arrives, nothing is added to the lifespan and no deferral occurs.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It has also been said concerning the meaning of the verse: it may be that it is decreed that a person's lifespan is a hundred years if he obeys and ninety if he disobeys; whichever of the two he reaches is in a Book.
﴿إِنَّ ذَلِكَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ﴾, that is, recording long and short lifespans is not difficult for Him.

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا يَسْتَوِي ٱلْبَحْرَانِ هَـٰذَا عَذْبٌ فُرَاتٌ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: الفُرَات is the sweetest of sweet [water], and الأُجَاج is the saltiest of salt.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَمِن كُلٍّ تَأْكُلُونَ لَحْماً طَرِيّاً وَتَسْتَخْرِجُونَ حِلْيَةً تَلْبَسُونَهَا﴾.
The ornament is pearls and coral, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُمَا اللُّؤْلُؤُ وَالمَرْجَانُ﴾, although they come out only from the salt [sea].
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is frequent in the speech of the Arabs: because the two seas are mixed, it is permissible to say "it comes out of both of them" although it comes out only of one of them — according to the view of some lexicographers.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَتَرَى ٱلْفُلْكَ فِيهِ مَوَاخِرَ لِتَبْتَغُواْ مِن فَضْلِهِ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, the ships run coming and going.
Abū Jaʿfar said: مَخَرتِ السفينةُ تَمْخُرُ and تَمْخَرُ, مَخْرَاً and مُخُوراً: when the ship cleaves the water.

nahhas-meani:13-13.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِهِ مَا يَمْلِكُونَ مِن قِطْمِيرٍ﴾.
Khuṣayf narrated from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: (al-qiṭmīr) is the thin skin on the date-stone, that is, between it and the date; "al-fatīl" is what is in the slit of the date-stone; and he said: "al-naqīr" is the speck in the middle of the date-stone.

nahhas-meani:14-14.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ يَكْفُرُونَ بِشِرْكِـكُمْ وَلاَ يُنَبِّئُكَ مِثْلُ خَبِيرٍ﴾.
That is, they disown them and their worship of them, and rebuke them for that.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَلاَ يُنَبِّئُكَ مِثْلُ خَبِيرٍ﴾: and He is Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, All-Aware of what will be, which no one but He knows.

nahhas-meani:18-18.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ﴾.
Simāk narrated from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: No one is taken to task for the sin of another.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَإِن تَدْعُ مُثْقَلَةٌ إِلَىٰ حِمْلِهَا لاَ يُحْمَلْ مِنْهُ شَيْءٌ﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿إِلَىٰ حِمْلِهَا﴾, that is, to the sins.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning is: and if a soul that sins have weighed down calls ﴿إِلَىٰ حِمْلِهَا﴾ — which is its sins — nothing of its load, which is its sins, will be carried.
﴿وَلَوْ كَانَ ذَا قُرْبَىٰ﴾, that is, even if the one whom it calls to that is a father, or a son, or the like.

nahhas-meani:19-21.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا يَسْتَوِي ٱلأَعْمَىٰ وَٱلْبَصِيرُ، وَلاَ ٱلظُّلُمَاتُ وَلاَ ٱلنُّورُ، وَلاَ ٱلظِّلُّ وَلاَ ٱلْحَرُورُ﴾ [Verses 19–21].
Qatāda said: That is, just as the blind and the seeing are not equal, the believer and the unbeliever are not equal.
Someone else said: The meaning is: not equal are the one blind to the truth, who is the unbeliever, and the one who sees guidance, who is the believer; ﴿وَلاَ ٱلظُّلُمَاتُ﴾, which are the errors, ﴿وَلاَ ٱلنُّورُ﴾, which is guidance.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَلاَ ٱلظِّلُّ وَلاَ ٱلْحَرُورُ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: ﴿ٱلْحَرُورُ﴾ in this place is only by day, with the sun.
And it is said: He means Paradise and the Fire.
And it is said: the one who is in the shade of the truth and the one who is in the scorching heat are not equal.
Al-Farrāʾ said: (al-ḥarūr) is constant heat, by night or by day, while al-samūm is by day specifically.
Ruʾba ibn al-ʿAjjāj said: ﴿ٱلْحَرُورُ﴾ is by night specifically, and al-samūm by day.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The view of Abū ʿUbayda is more likely, because shade is only spoken of on a sunny day.
